name: Project Osprey
one_liner: A security operations platform where a learning bot runs response playbooks across existing tools and analysts collaborate in a built-in chat war room.

buyer.company_profile: Enterprises and MSSPs with a staffed SOC running a SIEM, endpoint tools and firewalls from several vendors, struggling to hire analysts.

problem.summary: Every security product has its own API and console; customers lack a cross-product workflow. Analysts repeat the same enrichment and containment steps by hand, duplicate incidents pile up, and investigations are scattered over email and tickets with no audit trail. Qualified analysts are scarce, so response times grow.

evidence.claim: Incident management involves repeatable detection, analysis, containment and recovery steps that can be codified.
Security orchestration connects disparate security tools and automates workflows across them.
Security teams run many separate tools, each with its own interface.

why_now.summary: Most security products now expose APIs, chat-based collaboration (ChatOps) is mainstream in engineering, and the analyst shortage makes automation of routine response tasks a board-level concern.

features.feature: Integrations with SIEM, endpoint, firewall and threat-intel products using their own credentials
Playbook engine that runs enrichment and response tasks automatically on new incidents
Built-in chat war room where analysts and the bot run commands together
features.why: Collaboration plus a natural audit trail.

features.feature: Bot learns from analyst actions to suggest next steps and detect duplicate incidents
Ticketing, reporting and full audit log

competitors.name: Phantom
competitors.how_we_differ: Collaboration and learning built in, not only playbook automation.

competitors.name: IBM Resilient
competitors.how_we_differ: Automation-first with chat collaboration rather than a case-management workflow.

competitors.name: ServiceNow Security Operations
competitors.how_we_differ: Purpose-built for analysts with deep security integrations.

competitors.name: Swimlane
competitors.how_we_differ: Chat war room and bot that learns from analysts.

competitors.name: TheHive (free, open source)
competitors.how_we_differ: Automated response, not only case tracking.

differentiation: Combines orchestration, case management and real-time chat collaboration in one product, with a bot that both executes playbooks and learns from analysts, so it helps understaffed SOCs immediately and captures an audit trail automatically.

build.team: About 18 people: 4 security-industry founders, engineering in Israel, sales in the US
hardest_parts: Building and maintaining hundreds of integrations
Making machine learning suggestions accurate enough to be trusted

pricing.model: Annual subscription per analyst seat with integrations included; on-prem or cloud
pricing.entry_price: Working assumption: $50,000/year for up to 5 analysts
pricing.rationale: SOC tooling budgets are per-analyst and automation savings are easy to express in analyst-hours.

comparables.price: No public list price at the time (quote-based enterprise sale)

go_to_market.first_customers: Ten enterprises and MSSPs with 5-30 analyst SOCs using several major security vendors, recruited through beta users and founders' industry networks.
go_to_market.channel: Direct enterprise sales from a US office, technology alliances with security vendors whose products it integrates.
go_to_market.wedge: Automate phishing triage and duplicate-incident detection in the first weeks.

risks: SIEM and security platform vendors bundle orchestration
Crowded emerging category with well-funded rivals

riskiest_assumption.assumption: SOCs will adopt a chat-centred workflow and let a bot run response actions.
riskiest_assumption.test: Run the beta with 5 SOCs for 2 weeks and track how many incidents are handled through the war room and automated playbooks.
riskiest_assumption.success_signal: At least 50% of incidents in beta SOCs are handled in the platform and 3 beta users convert to paid.

open_questions: Will customers buy orchestration standalone or expect it in their SIEM?
How much of the bot's learning generalises across customers?
